newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Political infighting halts advance on Khmer Rouge.
newsitem.headline: Political infighting halts advance on Khmer Rouge.

text.p: Cambodian troops, demoralised by bickering between leaders of the ailing coalition government, have halted an advance on the last stronghold of Khmer Rouge guerrillas, a senior officer said on Thursday.
Senior commanders had ordered troops advancing on the northern rebel base of Anlong Veng to halt their push and focus on strengthening their own bases, said General Long Sereirath.
He believed the government would not be able to take the headquarters of up to 2,000 Khmer Rouge rebels loyal to hardliners Ta Mok and Pol Pot before the rainy season begins around the end of May.

The Maoist-inspired movement has been unravelling since former top official Ieng Sary split with Khmer Rouge hardliners last August and joined the government, triggering the defections of thousands of fighters.
"Ta Mok can live easily in his base for one more year," General Long Sereirath said by phone from the northwest province of Siem Reap.
"The morale of troops waiting in positions near Anlong Veng in preparation to take Ta Mok's base plummeted when they heard about the political crisis in Phnom Penh," said the general.

The royalist FUNCINPEC and the Cambodian People's Party (CPP) formed an uneasy coalition after U.N.-run elections in 1993. Tension between the two parties has soared since a deadly March 30 grenade attack on a demonstration in Phnom Penh led by opposition leader and FUNCINPEC ally, Sam Rainsy.

Relations deteriorated further last week after FUNCINPEC dissidents, including Siem Reap Governor Toan Chhay, challenged the leadership of royalist co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh with the full support of the CPP.
Ties between Ranariddh and co-Premier Hun Sen of the CPP have been strained for some time.
General Long Sereirath called on the armed forces in his key region to remain neutral and to avoid fighting.

"Before the armed forces seemed to be neutral, but when the crisis in Phnom Penh erupted the troops started separating and listening to their own commanders, so both sides are building up their muscle," he told Reuters.

The Khmer Rouge, which ruled Cambodia by terror during the 1975-79 "killing fields" regime, signed a U.N.-brokered peace pact in 1991. The guerrillas later reneged on the deal and have been fighting the coalition government formed in 1993.

FUNCINPEC officials have tried to negotiate the defection of the feared one-legged commander Ta Mok. But earlier this month said they would attack Anlong Veng after receiving news that 12 members of a government negotiating team had been killed.
